Phase 2. Design and implement based on the Gherkin specification.

---

## Context-dependent behaviour

| Context | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First cycle | Full design and implementation |
| Later cycles | Reflect the design of affected parts and fix the implementation |

---

## Implementation basis

Use the GWT (Gherkin) of approved scenarios as the basis for functional behaviour.
Do not arbitrarily add behaviour not included in the Gherkin.
Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
scenarios' GWT specifications. Develop the production code in `implementation/`,
separately from the exploration code in `prototypes/`.

This restriction applies to exploration code, including prototypes made in later
cycles. Later cycles may modify the existing production implementation according
to the updated approved GWT; they do not require rebuilding it from scratch.

---

## Internal information system

Accumulate the following information during implementation. Keep the format
lightweight, but at a level that enables impact analysis in later cycles.

### Design-decision record
What was decided, why, and which alternatives were dropped.
Notes for understanding the structure after context is reset.

### Scenario-code mapping
Which scenario (SCN-NNN) corresponds to which code.
The basis for judging the impact scope on a change request.

### Tests
Create tests together with the implementation.
Include both Gherkin-based acceptance tests and internal unit/integration tests.

---

## Sufficiency criteria

The internal information system is sufficient when it meets both of:
- A level that enables impact analysis in later cycles
- A level from which, if the user requests traditional artifacts (design
  documents, test plans, etc.), they can be generated and provided

---

## Transition to Phase 3

When implementation and test creation are complete, switch to Phase 3
(verification).

## Gherkin
Feature: Saving bookmarks

  Scenario: Save a new web address
    Given the personal bookmark collection is empty
    And a web address is in the save field
    When the user chooses to save the link
    Then the app saves one bookmark for that web address
    And the bookmark contains the page title and description obtained by the app
    And the bookmark appears under "Recently saved"

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Saving bookmarks

  Scenario: Correct an obtained title before saving
    Given the app has obtained a title and description for a new web address
    When the user replaces the obtained title before saving
    And saves the link
    Then the bookmark is saved with the replacement title
    And the obtained description is preserved

  Scenario: Correct an obtained description before saving
    Given the app has obtained a title and description for a new web address
    When the user replaces the obtained description before saving
    And saves the link
    Then the bookmark is saved with the replacement description
    And the obtained title is preserved

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Saving bookmarks

  Scenario: Recognize an already-saved web address
    Given one bookmark exists for a web address
    And the bookmark has a title corrected by the user
    When the user asks the app to get details for the same web address
    Then the collection still contains one bookmark for that web address
    And the app explains that the link was already saved
    And the app brings the existing bookmark into focus
    And the corrected title remains unchanged

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Finding bookmarks

  Scenario Outline: Narrow bookmarks using remembered words
    Given the collection contains bookmarks with titles, descriptions, personal notes, and web addresses
    When the user types a word found only in a bookmark's <field>
    Then the results immediately narrow to include that bookmark
    And the result is displayed as its normal bookmark card
    And no field-match explanation is added to the card

    Examples:
      | field         |
      | title         |
      | description   |
      | personal note |
      | web address   |

  Scenario: Keep multiple search results in collection order
    Given multiple bookmarks contain the user's search words
    When the user types those words
    Then all matching bookmarks are shown
    And they remain ordered newest first

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Personal bookmark notes

  Scenario: Add a formatted note to a bookmark
    Given a saved bookmark has no personal note
    When the user adds a note directly on its card
    And applies bold text, a bulleted list, or a link using the formatting bar
    And saves the note
    Then the formatted note is displayed on that bookmark card
    And the note is associated only with that bookmark
    And words in the note can be used to find the bookmark

  Scenario: Edit a personal note later
    Given a saved bookmark has a personal note
    When the user opens that note for editing from its card
    And changes and saves the note
    Then the changed formatted note is displayed on that bookmark card

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Organizing bookmarks with labels

  Scenario: View all bookmarks carrying a label
    Given saved bookmarks carry labels
    And some bookmarks carry more than one label
    When the user selects a label from the row above the collection
    Then only bookmarks carrying that label are shown
    And the label shows the number of bookmarks carrying it
    And bookmarks carrying other labels as well remain included

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Organizing bookmarks with labels

  Scenario: Reuse an existing label while saving
    Given an existing label is already used by saved bookmarks
    And the user is reviewing a new bookmark before saving
    When the user types part of the existing label name
    Then the matching label is suggested with its bookmark count
    When the user selects the suggestion and saves the bookmark
    Then the label is displayed on the saved bookmark card

  Scenario: Create a new label while saving
    Given the user is reviewing a new bookmark before saving
    When the user enters a label name that does not match an existing label

    Then the new label is selected on the bookmark before saving

  Scenario: Revise labels later
    Given a saved bookmark carries one or more labels
    When the user opens the bookmark for editing
    Then its labels remain visibly selected in the review fields
    And the user can add or remove labels

  Scenario: Open the Read later collection

    And the number of waiting bookmarks is displayed

    Given a saved bookmark is shown in Read later
    When the user marks it done

    And the Read later count decreases

  Scenario: Page details cannot be obtained

  Scenario: No bookmarks match a search

    And the app states that no saved links match

Feature: Reading list

  Scenario: All read-later bookmarks have been completed
    Given saved bookmarks exist in All bookmarks
    And no bookmarks remain marked Read later
    When the user opens Read later

    And the view says the user is all caught up

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Bookmark card boundaries

  Scenario: Read a long formatted note
    Given a bookmark has a long personal note containing supported formatting
    When the bookmark is shown in the collection
    Then the note is initially folded on its card
    When the user chooses to show the full note
    Then the note expands in place
    And its bold text, bulleted lists, and links remain formatted
    When the user chooses to show less
    Then the note folds again

  Scenario: Display many labels on one bookmark
    Given a bookmark carries enough labels to exceed one line
    When its card is shown
    Then the labels wrap onto additional lines
    And the card remains usable

## Gherkin
Feature: Preventing duplicate bookmarks

  Scenario: Enter an exact saved address again
    Given a bookmark exists for a web address with user-authored details
    When the user enters the exact same address again
    Then no duplicate bookmark is created
    And the existing bookmark is shown
    And its user-authored title, note, and labels remain unchanged

  Scenario: Enter a confidently equivalent address
    Given a bookmark exists for a web address
    When the user enters an address that differs only by a safely recognized trailing slash or referral addition
    Then no duplicate bookmark is created
    And the existing bookmark is shown unchanged

  Scenario: Address equivalence is uncertain
    Given a bookmark exists for a web address
    When the user enters a different address that cannot be confidently identified as the same page
    Then the app does not merge it with the existing bookmark

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Organizing bookmarks with labels

  Scenario Outline: Reuse an existing label despite an insignificant variation
    Given the label "Cooking" already exists
    When the user enters <entered label> for a bookmark
    Then the existing "Cooking" label is suggested
    And a second label is not created

    Examples:
      | entered label |
      | cooking       |
      | " Cooking"   |
      | "Cooking "   |

## Assumptions
## Gherkin
Feature: Preserving saved bookmarks

  Scenario: The webpage changes after saving
    Given a bookmark has saved details and user-authored changes
    When the webpage later changes its title or description
    Then the saved title and description remain unchanged
    And the personal note and labels remain unchanged

  Scenario: The webpage disappears after saving
    Given a bookmark has a saved title, description, personal note, and labels

    Then the bookmark remains in the collection
    And its saved title, description, personal note, and labels remain available

Phase 4. Present the result to the user and obtain acceptance confirmation.

---

## Acceptance procedure

### Presenting the result

Present the implemented software to the client and report that verification
against the approved scenarios' GWT specifications and the internal tests has
passed. Summarise the verification outcome in plain language and provide access
to the implemented software.

For the first cycle, the report covers all approved scenarios. For later cycles,
it covers the changed scenarios and affected existing scenarios.

### Acceptance confirmation

Ask the client to accept the implemented software as a whole on the basis of
the approved behaviour and the verification report. Acceptance completes the
development work for the cycle.

### Handling client requests

Use the requirement scenarios approved during Phase 1 as the baseline. Classify
each request by whether fulfilling it changes that baseline:

- Implementation error: the implementation does not satisfy an approved
  scenario. Return to Phase 2, fix the implementation, repeat verification in
  Phase 3, and request acceptance again. Preserve the approved scenario.
- Requirement change or addition: fulfilling the request requires changing an
  approved scenario or adding a scenario. Record the request for the next cycle
  in context/session-log.md, retaining the current approved scenarios.

Explain the classification using the previously approved behaviour in plain
language. If the client's request is unclear, clarify whether the software fails
to perform that behaviour or the desired behaviour has changed. Keep requirement
exploration within Phase 1 of the cycle that will address the change.

After recording a requirement change or addition, ask for acceptance of the
current software, for example:
"I've recorded that request for the next cycle. The software implements the
behaviour we approved, and its verification is complete. Do you accept this
software and agree to complete this cycle?"

Wait for the client's explicit acceptance. A request recorded for a later cycle
does not itself constitute acceptance of the current software.

---

## Transition to idle

When acceptance confirmation is complete, switch to the idle state. In this
experiment, the trial ends after acceptance of the first cycle. Retain requests
for later cycles in the session log.

---

## Session log

On acceptance completion, record the following in the session log:
- List of accepted scenarios
- Cycle number
- Acceptance result (approved / partially approved / rejected)
- Requirement changes or additions recorded for a later cycle
